## Physical scenario

A small speck of dust with mass $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ $g$ has fallen into the hole shown in figure and appears to be at rest.

## Question

What is the deepest hole of this width from which it would have a good chance to escape?

## Answer choices

- A: A: $1.0 \times 10^{-27}$ $m$

- B: B: $1.2 \times 10^{-27}$ $m$

- C: C: $1.4 \times 10^{-27}$ $m$

- D: D: $1.6 \times 10^{-27}$ $m$

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image shows a cross-sectional diagram of a curved, trough-like structure with a frictionless surface. 

- There is a small black dot positioned at the center of this trough, representing an object.
- The trough has smooth, symmetrical walls, indicating a gradual rise on both sides.
- The height of the trough is marked as "1.0 μm" on the right side.
- The width of the trough at its widest point is specified as "10 μm" along the bottom.
- A label pointing to the surface states "Frictionless surface."

The overall depiction suggests a scenario where the object can move back and forth due to the frictionless nature of the surface.
